title: Why AI for MBA students, and the three levels of AI learning
summary: The four reasons and the numbers behind why MBA students need AI, plus what the Basic, Intermediate and Advanced levels of AI learning cover.

chunks.heading: AI in the curriculum and what employers want
chunks.explanation_md:
The deck opens with a simple question: **why should MBA students care about AI?** The first two reasons are about schools and jobs.

**1. Awareness & curriculum integration.** Over **75% of business schools** worldwide (including India and the U.S.) now weave AI into their curricula, from tutoring to strategy and career guidance. Leading schools like **Wharton, Kogod, Columbia, Duke, Stanford and Harvard** actively embed AI tools into core subjects.

**2. AI skills demand.**
- **74% of employers** specifically look for **AI/ML proficiency** in MBA grads. That lifted AI from **21st to 4th** among sought-after competencies (e-GMAT).
- **66% of organizational leaders** won't hire candidates lacking **AI literacy** (Microsoft CDN).
- Recruiters note **AI fluency** is now expected more than ever, especially for roles involving **strategy and operations** (AI Literacy Institute).
chunks.exam_line: Over 75% of business schools weave AI into curricula; 74% of employers seek AI/ML skills in MBA grads (AI rose from 21st to 4th); 66% of leaders won't hire without AI literacy.

chunks.heading: How students use AI, and where the gaps are
chunks.explanation_md:
**3. Practical usage & engagement.** Students use AI **weekly, if not daily**, for essay writing, brainstorming, data analysis, simulations and more. The summary table puts numbers on it: **82% use AI weekly** and **39% daily** (Microsoft CDN, DataCamp).

Schools report **AI-enabled projects, workshops and hackathons**, for example **datathons with Bloomberg and Amazon**, to boost hands-on experience (Study International).

**4. Gaps & challenges.** Adoption is high, but **formal training remains inconsistent**. A UK study shows only **36% of students** receive **institutional support** in 2025. MBA programs also face a **lack of strategy**, **ethics integration** and **equipment** for deep AI use.

The slide's summary table has five rows: **curriculum integration** (about 75% of MBA programs), **employer demand** (74% and 66%), **student usage** (82% weekly, 39% daily), **formal training availability** (only about 36%) and **practical engagement** (projects, workshops, competitions, real-world AI tasks).
chunks.exam_line: Students: 82% use AI weekly and 39% daily, but only about 36% get institutional support, so formal training is the gap.

chunks.heading: Basic level: AI literacy for non-tech learners
chunks.explanation_md:
The deck then lays out **three levels of AI learning**. The first is the **Basic Level (AI Literacy / Non-Tech Background)**, for professionals, students or government officers learning **AI fundamentals**.

What it covers:
- Introduction to AI and its applications
- Types of AI: **Narrow AI**
- **Key concepts: Data, Algorithms, Models, Bias, Ethics**
- AI in sectors: **Agriculture, Healthcare, Education, Governance**
- Intro to **NLP** (language), **Computer Vision (CV)** and **speech recognition** AI
- **Responsible AI**, fairness and data privacy
- Tools: **Google Colab** and AI-powered apps (**ChatGPT, Gemini** etc.)
chunks.exam_line: Basic level (AI literacy): key concepts are Data, Algorithms, Models, Bias, Ethics; tools are Google Colab and AI apps like ChatGPT and Gemini.

check_questions.explanation: The Basic Level is for professionals, students or government officers learning AI fundamentals. The Advanced level is for aspiring AI engineers and researchers.

chunks.heading: Intermediate level: building simple models
chunks.explanation_md:
The **Intermediate Level (Students / Practitioners)** is for those **building or deploying simple models**. It covers:
- Data collection, cleaning & preprocessing
- **Supervised vs unsupervised learning**
- Machine learning
- **Model training (regression, classification)**
- Scikit-learn, TensorFlow, PyTorch basics
- Working with datasets: CSVs, images, text
- **Validation, testing, overfitting**
- Projects: AI for **crop disease**, **traffic prediction**, **sentiment analysis**
chunks.exam_line: Intermediate level: data cleaning, supervised vs unsupervised learning, regression and classification, Scikit-learn, TensorFlow and PyTorch basics, validation and overfitting.

clarification.text: In supervised learning the model learns from examples that come with the right answers (labels); in unsupervised learning it looks for patterns in data that has no labels.

chunks.heading: Advanced / developer level
chunks.explanation_md:
The **Advanced / Developer Level** is for **aspiring AI engineers and researchers**:
- **Deep learning: CNNs, RNNs, Transformers**
- **Model optimization**: loss functions, gradient descent, hyperparameter tuning
- Frameworks: advanced PyTorch, TensorFlow, HuggingFace
- **Transfer learning, embeddings, foundation models**
- **Deployment**: ONNX, APIs, edge deployment
- **MLOps**, versioning, reproducibility
- Real-world applications with scale: **chatbots, recommendation engines, autonomous systems**

So the ladder is: basic = learning AI fundamentals; intermediate = building or deploying simple models; advanced = aspiring AI engineers and researchers.
chunks.exam_line: Advanced level: deep learning (CNNs, RNNs, Transformers), model optimization, transfer learning and foundation models, deployment and MLOps.
